- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.36) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast drop, it often overcorrects; cap peak forecast at 2–3% above recent high.
- In low sentiment (≤0.18) periods, model underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast for next 7–14 days to avoid under-shock.
- Model often underestimates early in 30-day horizon; apply 1–2% upward bias for first 5–7 days if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- If sentiment history shows recent volatility (e.g., alternating 0.36/0.18), model tends to lag; adjust forecast to align with 3–5 day moving average of true values.
- When sentiment is high and price is falling, model often fails to anticipate reversal; add 0.5–1.5% upward bias for next 3–5 days to capture mean reversion.
